D.t: Xavier Becerra leads by 26.2 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 3,532,164 votes; a one point swing is about 67,485 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +19.6 and D +32.9. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +23.7. Your best recent poll is Emerson College at D +27.7; your worst is David Wolfson for Hilton (R) at D +9.1. 12 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Los Angeles, a projected net 1,276,254 votes; Alameda, a projected net 351,953 votes; Santa Clara, a projected net 283,509 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Orange, D +5.3, 8.7% of the vote; Riverside, D +11.0, 5.7% of the vote; Fresno, R +0.5, 2.1% of the vote; San Joaquin, D +7.2, 1.7% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Xavier Becerra runs furthest behind in Placer, Santa Barbara, Ventura. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 56% of voters, 55 to 45, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.81 points; College graduates, 46% of voters, 60 to 39, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.31 points; Men, 46% of voters, 57 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.30 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Xavier Becerra: Immigration voters 34 to 65, Incomes $125K and up 54 to 45, White voters 55 to 45. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$6.2M cash against $2.1M. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.3 points toward Xavier Becerra. Bank it: chase the remaining mail ballots and low propensity voters who have not voted.
Money: Raised $21.4M against $29.7M for Xavier Becerra.
